STEP 01

Install The Video Shotcraft Skill

Get the Skill from Finch, hand it to your Agent, then load the shot cards, template, components, audio assets, and workflow notes into the current environment.

Install in 3 steps
  • 1 · Find it on FinchOpen Video Shotcraft on Finch. Confirm the product name video-shotcraft-finchip-new and the current version 1, then follow the on-page steps.
  • 2 · Get the fileDownload the Skill package and stay signed in for the whole download so it completes.
  • 3 · Hand it to your AgentImport it in Claude Code or Codex, then reopen or refresh the workspace and confirm the Skill is available.
INSTALL PROMPT
I have downloaded the Video Shotcraft skill package from Finch. Please install it into this workspace, then confirm that the skill instructions, shot cards, template, components, and audio assets are all loaded.
STEP 02

Prepare The Input Assets

Assets
Project entryProject directory or webpage URL
Visual assetsScreenshots / screen recordings / images / audio
Written assetsProduct copy or supporting notes

This example uses an HTML file with embedded images and written content.

Gather the source cards

Capture the cards from the working Margin prototype. In the film, check that each card title can be read and that the three arrivals are distinct.

STEP 03

Write A Clear Production Prompt

Describe the assets, theme, focus points, and delivery requirements in one complete request.

Ready to adapt

This example does not choose a mode in advance. Following the skill workflow, the Agent first performs a read-only review of the product page and assets, then recommends the best route for the project goal.

PRODUCTION PROMPT
Using video-shotcraft's autonomous creative mode, create a promotional video for my product's official website (page URL or local project directory here). Focus on showcasing the number of shots available, category search, animated sample cards, and the ability to go from a single prompt to a complete promotional video. Use publicly available page data and keep the video length between 20 and 30 seconds.
STEP 04

Choose A Production Mode

If a mode is specified, the Agent runs it directly. If no mode is specified, the Agent first reviews the product page and assets, then recommends a route.

  • 01 · Template modeDirect template useReuse the Ink Press shot structure while replacing product screenshots, copy, and brand details. Best for quickly adapting a proven template film.
  • 02 · Autonomous creationAutonomous free creationLet the Agent decide the visual direction, shot plan, storyboard, asset capture, sound design, and final render.
  • 03 · Guided co-creationGuided co-creationReview the visual direction, shot mapping, and final storyboard in stages. Best when the project has a clear preferred message or creative direction.
MODE PROMPT
I want to use [Template mode / Autonomous creation / Guided co-creation] for this video. If I have not selected a mode, first perform a read-only review of the product page and assets. Explain whether the Ink Press template, autonomous creation, and guided co-creation are each suitable, then recommend one route before continuing.
STEP 05

Organize Pages And Assets

Video Shotcraft is not about generating fake UI. It is about filming real product pages with a strong sense of camera work. Confirm page states, data boundaries, and text clarity before production.

Before capture
  • Real pagesWhen showcasing the product, prioritize real pages, real screenshots, or real screen recordings. Fake UI is only suitable for abstract openings or standalone components.
  • Page statesPrepare clear and reproducible states for each feature, such as input, processing, result, detail, and export screens.
  • ClarityCheck screenshot resolution to avoid blurry text, cropping, obstruction, or replacement mistakes after zooming.
  • Data safetyFreeze demo data. Redact sensitive content before capture and production.

Capture both assignment states

Capture the palette with Maya highlighted, then run the assignment. Check the assignee chip and event in the same conversation.

STEP 06

Confirm Output Files

A complete delivery is more than one mp4. It is a video project that can be reviewed, adjusted, and iterated.

Delivery checklist
  • Project folderRemotion project, assets, timeline, design notes, and reproducible render configuration.
  • Two final cutsA version with BGM, plus a version without BGM that keeps SFX for easier music replacement later.
  • QA notesKeyframe checks, final review notes, sensitive information checks, and render parameters.
  • Motion workbenchShots, captions, transitions, and sound effects are split into visual tracks for further tuning and export.

Record the delivery frame times

Export stills from the final MP4 and record their timestamps so reviewers can verify the ice selection carried through to the cart.

STEP 07

Final QA Checklist

Before delivery, confirm that the video truly introduces the product: clear to read, easy to understand, steady in rhythm, held on key points, and free of sensitive information leaks.

Send to your Agent for further iteration
  • ThemeDoes the video clearly explain the product, audience, and value instead of only walking through operations?
  • ShotsDoes it follow the intended structure, does each shot express one action, and do key details get enough hold time?
  • VisualsIs page text legible, with no obstruction, cropping, distortion, or replacement mistakes?
  • SoundAre voiceover, BGM, and SFX balanced, and does the music avoid covering voice or key information?
  • DeliveryWere both final cuts exported, was an independent final review completed, and was sensitive information cleared?
REVISION PROMPT
Please keep optimizing the video based on the current version: check whether the theme is clear, whether the shots follow the structure, whether page text is legible, whether key information has enough hold time, and whether BGM or SFX covers the voice. Re-export both the version with BGM and the version without BGM. If you find sensitive information, obstruction, cropping, or replacement mistakes, fix them before rendering.
